Nārycĭon , ii, n., = Ναρύκιον, Plin. 4, 17, 12, § 27; and Nāryx , ycis, f., = Νάρυξ,
I.a city of the Ozolian Locrians, a colony from which built the city of Locri, in Italy, Plin. 4, 17, 12, § 27 (Jan. Narycum).—Hence, Nārycĭus , a, um, adj., = Ναρύκιος, of or belonging to the city of Narycion (the birthplace of Ajax Oïleus), Narycian: “hic et Narycii posuerunt moenia Locri (cf. Narycion),” Verg. A. 3, 399 : “pix,” id. G. 2, 438 : “Lelex,” a king of the Locrians, Ov. M. 8, 312 : “heros,” i. e. the son of Ajax Oïleus, who led the colony of Locrians to Italy, id. ib. 14, 468 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
